newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: New Madagascar leader to lead Washington visit.
newsitem.headline: New Madagascar leader to lead Washington visit.

text.p: The interim president of Madagascar said on Saturday he would lead a team to Washington mid this month to seek funding to reverse what the IMF managing director has described as shocking economic decline.

Prime Minister Norbert Ratsirahonana was designated interim president by the Indian Ocean island's constituonal court on Thursday after the court confirmed the impeachment of President Albert Zafy. He will serve until a presidential election.

Ratsirahonana, in remarks broadcast on state radio, said he would discuss with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Madagascar's economic reform programme and the possible shelving of its external debt.
Ratsirahonana's delegation leaves Antananarivo for Washington in mid September.

In an address to the nation, Zafy said he would step down on October 10 but he hit out at the head of the national assembly, Richard Andriamanjato, and the 99 deputies who voted for impeachment. He blamed his ouster on a political clique opposed to his policies.
Zafy accused Andriamanjato of backing a plan to dump toxic waste in Madagascar in return for up to $300 million and for supporting "parallel financing" opposed by the IMF.
He criticised parliamentarians for earning high salaries compared with the general poverty of the Malagasy people.
Before the court ruling, the next presidential election was scheduled for 1998, a year after parliamentary polls.
The managing director of the IMF said during a visit earlier this year that he was shocked by Madagascar's economic decline since his last trip in 1991.
Before the visit Zafy had defended "parallel financing" -- private loans ostensibly for development projects but at higher interest rates than from multilateral donors such as the IMF.
Madagascar last month signed undertakings with the IMF and World Bank on reforms expected to pave the way for a three-year Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility and debt rescheduling.
Madagascar has a total foreign debt of some $4 billion.
